claims: The Strait of Hormuz is approximately 21–30 miles wide.
The Strait of Hormuz connects the Persian Gulf to the Gulf of Oman.
The Strait of Hormuz is located between Iran and Oman.
Roughly 20% of global oil passes through the Strait of Hormuz daily.
Roughly 20% of global liquefied natural gas (LNG) passes through the Strait of Hormuz daily.
The Strait of Hormuz is the primary route for oil exports from Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE.
Oil exports from Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, and the UAE via the Strait of Hormuz are largely bound for Asian markets.

Iran frequently uses the Strait of Hormuz as a strategic lever to pressure Western powers, often threatening or conducting partial closures or attacks on shipping, as noted in the Al Jazeera and The Conversation reports.
U.S. and regional naval forces maintain a constant presence in the Strait of Hormuz, as discussed on Wikipedia.
U.S. and regional naval forces manage a traffic separation scheme (TSS) for safe passage in the Strait of Hormuz, as discussed on Wikipedia.
The Strait of Hormuz serves as the only sea passage from the Persian Gulf to the open ocean.
